question: Why do colon bacteria that make vitamin B12 not spare vegans from needing supplements?
answer: Because they make it downstream of the exit. B12 is absorbed at the far end of the small intestine, bound to intrinsic factor, a carrier protein made by the stomach. The colon comes after that point, so vitamin made there leaves in the faeces, much of it in forms human cells cannot use.
move: A supply is useless if it arrives past the point of collection.
ask: What supply do I count on that arrives past the point where I can collect it?
reference: Degnan, Taga & Goodman, Vitamin B12 as a modulator of gut microbial ecology, Cell Metabolism, 2014
